title: Data Governance Rules
purpose: Bound data-related work across contracts, validation, transformations, privacy, persistence, migrations, and testing.

rules.statement: Identify the exact data boundary before making changes: input, output, storage, transport, transformation, display, or deletion.
Do not inspect unrelated production data, logs, exports, databases, backups, analytics stores, schemas, migrations, fixtures, APIs, or transforms.
Preserve field names, types, nullability, units, encoding, time zone, identifiers, ordering, and cardinality unless the requirement changes them.
Document contract changes in API docs, schema docs, data model docs, migration notes, or operational docs.
Validate incoming and outgoing data at system boundaries such as APIs, file exports, queues, event streams, reports, or persistence boundaries.
Do not silently accept malformed data or silently drop fields, records, or errors.
Prefer structured parsers for structured formats such as JSON, YAML, CSV, XML, TOML, SQL, HTML, known logs, messages, events, and reports.

Do not expose secrets, credentials, tokens, personal data, protected records, customer data, or internal-only identifiers in logs, prompts, generated examples, fixtures, screenshots, or documentation.
Schema, migration, retention, deletion, and backfill changes require explicit requirement coverage and should be reversible where possible.
Test changed data behavior, validation paths, edge cases, representative success cases, and destructive or privacy-sensitive behavior when applicable.
